title: the Console projection carries the real Session and the real permission identity the agent daemon's engine holds
gate_status_note: The gate is declared and its measured source evidence is green. It stays partial because sessionEvents is not projected, the notification title is a fixed Console label, the projection also carries the daemon's own readiness-channel Session, a hard crash leaves the last observation projected, and this unit has no installed-copy, restart, deployed-entrypoint or cross-device receipt.
governing_decision: No control-to-agent channel exists and none is added: the control daemon declares no Teams listener. The agent daemon that owns the AcpHost facts is the only writer of one durable observation record per agent, and the control daemon is the only reader. The Console never enters the data path and no protocol frame changed.

black_box.topology:
one real control daemon through the real CLI (control start --config) on a real loopback port, one real `agentteams --serve opencode --ip 127.0.0.1 --port

--config` agent daemon with a real engine child, a real Newline-delimited ACP connection held by the driver as the controller, and a local OpenAI-compatible stub provider for the engine.
proven: no observation record exists before any Session is opened (honest absence, not an empty placeholder)
the published Session id is the one the engine really returned, and the published permission row carries the real controller-visible callback id with notificationId derived from it
an unchanged observation keeps its revision across a quiet window, so a poll is not a heartbeat
the control daemon's real GET /api/v1/projection carries the Session row and the pending notification row with the real permissionId, the real sessionId, kind permission and state pending
the real GET /api/v1/events SSE stream delivers a snapshot that carries those rows
an unauthenticated projection read is refused 401
the control daemon data directory holds no observation record, so there is one writer
answering the callback over ACP removes the permission row at a later revision while the Session row stays
closing the controller channel releases exactly that channel's Session, and the Sessions other open channels own stay reported (a real finding: the daemon's readiness channel owns its own Session)
SIGTERM on the agent daemon makes it publish the empty observation, and the control daemon then projects neither Session nor permission

full_suite.conclusion: NOT green. The failing set is unstable and lies in specs this change does not touch. cli/agentteams.spec.ts has a deterministic pre-existing cause: its beforeAll runs pnpm build:runtime while the parallel cli/package-install.spec.ts beforeAll runs pnpm build, and both delete and rebuild generated/runtime-lib. Both hooks exist at origin/main and git diff origin/main for both files is empty. Run in isolation, the three failing specs pass: 74 passed / 3 files, exit 0 (regression-failing-specs-isolated.log). Therefore these failures are environmental load and a pre-existing derived-artifact race, and this unit does not claim a green full regression.
